QuestionStmt.S: If a random variable $X$ has the p.d.f. $$f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{k}{x^2 + 1}, & \text{if } 0 < x < \infty \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$ then c.d.f. of $X$ is

Solution.S:
For the p.d.f. to be valid, the total probability must be 1:

$$\int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{k}{x^2+1} \, dx = 1$$

$$\Rightarrow k \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{x^2+1} \, dx = 1$$

We know that $$\int \frac{1}{x^2+1} \, dx = \tan^{-1} x + c.$$

Thus, $$k \left[ \tan^{-1} x \right]_{0}^{\infty} = 1$$

$$\Rightarrow k \left( \tan^{-1} \infty - \tan^{-1} 0 \right) = 1$$

Since $\tan^{-1} \infty = \frac{\pi}{2}$ and $\tan^{-1} 0 = 0$, we get:

$$k \left( \frac{\pi}{2} - 0 \right) = 1 \quad \Rightarrow \quad k = \frac{2}{\pi}.$$

The cumulative distribution function (c.d.f.) is given by:

$$F(x) = \int_{0}^{x} f(t) \, dt = \int_{0}^{x} \frac{2/\pi}{t^2+1} \, dt$$

$$= \frac{2}{\pi} \left[ \tan^{-1} t \right]_{0}^{x} = \frac{2}{\pi} \left( \tan^{-1} x - \tan^{-1} 0 \right) = \frac{2}{\pi} \tan^{-1} x.$$

Hence the correct option is C: $\frac{2}{\pi} \tan^{-1} x$.
